DESCRIPTION: Aerial photograph (CUCAP AVL 95) shows a cropmark of a fosse of circular enclosure (est. max diam. c. 25m). Either a ring-barrow or ringfort site.

Aerial photograph (CUCAP BGN 41) shows a cropmark of circular enclosure defined by fosse (est max diam c. 26m). Probably a ringfort site.

Date of upload: 8 September 2016

Aerial photograph (CUCAP BGN 50) shows a cropmark of a fosse defining a circular enclosure (est. max diam. c. 25m). It may be either a ringfort or ring-barrow.


Date of upload: 15 September 2016

Aerial photographs (CUCAP ASU 61, 62) show a cropmark of a fosse of circular enclosure (est. max diam. c. 40m). Possibly barrow or ringfort.

Date of upload: 15 September 2016

IFC Schools MSS (Vol. 657, 226) mentions a fort called 'Lios Luimneach'. No reliable remains visible in 1968 (SMR file).

Compiled by: Claire Breen

Date of upload: 9 November 2011

Identified on OS (1995) aerial photography as a double-ditched, sub-circular enclosure. Local tradition of fort on the site (pers. comm. Mr Colin Byrne, Briarleas, County Meath).

Compiled by Geraldine Stout

Date of upload: 13/03/2012

In dense scrubland. Marked on the 1838 edition of the OS 6-inch map as a circular enclosure (diam. c. 30m).
No visible surface trace survives. 

Compiled by: Galway Archaeological Survey, UCG

Date of upload: 22 July 2019

In pastureland. Marked on the 1838 edition of the of 6-inch map as a circular enclosure (diam. c. 23m). No visible surface trace survives. 

Compiled by: Galway Archaeological Survey, UCG

Date of upload: 23 July 2019

Known locally as a ringfort, located c. 25m south-west of a standing stone (CO141-043---). The area is overgrown with bushes and brambles and could not be accessed.  

Compiled by: Matt Kelleher

Date of upload/revision: 7 March 2022

Named 'fort' and hachured on 1843 OS 6-inch map. The site is identified in the field as a slightly sunken area (dims.20m NW-SE; 27m NE-SW; D 0.3m). There is no bank visible (Ua Broin 1944, 74, 202).
Compiled by Geraldine Stout

On inspection in 1989 a section of curving bank thought to be part of an ringfort was identified (pers. comm. Marcus Nolan).
Compiled by: Geraldine Stout

Date of upload: 26 August 2011

On the N bank of the river Dodder. Shown as a hachured enclosure(c. diam.20m) on the 1st edition OS 6-inch map (1843). Listed (No. 25) in the Dublin City Development Plan(1991) as 'Clonskeagh, site of fort'. Now occupied by Ramleh Park housing estate.

One of three sites within close proximity named 'fort' on the 1837 OS 6-inch map. There is a housing estate on the site. Not visible at ground level.

Compiled by: Geraldine Stout

Updated by: Christine Baker

Date of upload: 19 January 2015

Shown on OS 1909 6' sheet as an approximately triangular remnant of an enclosure (dims. c. 40 x 30 x 40), with hachures indicating a fosse at the NE side. No visible surface trace. Probably a ringfort site.

Date of upload: 15 September 2016

Site of a quarry. Depicted on first edition of the OS 6-inch map as a circular enclosure, possible ringfort that has now been quarried.

Compiled by: Caimin O'Brien

Date of upload: 17 December 2007

Situated on a prominent hill under pasture. Marked as an enclosure on the 1843 OS 6-inch map (max. diam c. 25m). Mentioned by Ua Broin (1941, 25). Not visible at ground level.
Compiled by: Geraldine Stout and Padraig Clancy
Revised upload on: 7 July 2018
There is no sign of the 'Fort' marked on the 1st and 2nd editions of the OS 6-inch maps. It was situated on a small hillock in excellent land with good views.

There is now no trace of the single-ringed 'Fort' marked on the 1st edition of the OS 6-inch map. A previous record (NMI) suggests it was 150 ft. in diameter. It is located on the SE slope of a hill in good land.

This possible ringfort was identified on Lidar (pers. comm. Dr Stephen Davis, UCD School of Archaeology).

Compiled by Geraldine Stout
Date of upload: 15/03/2012

Visible on aerial photographs (GSI S134, 135, 176, 177) as a cropmark enclosing a circular area (est. max diam. c. 55m). Probably a ringfort site.
